svg.text: AUTOCOMPLETE — WALKING THE TRIE FOR suggest("ca", 3)
one node per character · prefixes are SHARED, never duplicated
whole branch skipped: root.children.get('c') took us the other way
the subtree collectCandidates DFS-walks — S = 5 words
children: Map<Character, TrieNode> — the edge label IS the map key, not a field
endOfWord: boolean — the double ring above. "car" is a word AND a prefix of "card"
word: String — cached at terminal nodes so the DFS never rebuilds it from the path
frequency: int — re-adding a word does frequency += delta, O(L), no dedupe pass
"car" / "card" / "care" / "cat" / "cab" share 2 nodes ⇒ that sharing is the whole point of a trie ✓
removeWord("cab") would clear the flag then prune node 'b' on the way up, because it has no children left
node = root → children.get('c') → children.get('a') ⇒ the "ca" node
Any missing link returns null ⇒ getSuggestions returns an EMPTY list (no exception).
Cost depends on the prefix length only — not on how many words are in the trie ✓
empty prefix ("") is legal and starts the DFS at root — i.e. it walks EVERY word
STEP 2 · collectCandidates — full DFS of the subtree
visits 5 terminal nodes: car(5) · card(9) · care(7) · cat(12) · cab(4)
Each becomes new Suggestion(word, freq, score = freq) and is offered to the heap.
Visit ORDER is HashMap iteration order — undefined. Fine here, because the heap
+ the strategy's tie-break on word make the final answer deterministic anyway.
This DFS is the expensive part: O(S) where S = words under the prefix. Prefix "c" would be worse; "" walks all.
STEP 3 · bounded MIN-heap of size limit=3 — keeps the top-k in O(S log k)
offer → if size > limit, poll() drops the SMALLEST frequency
heap of size k, not a sort of size S ⇒ O(S log k) instead of O(S log S) ✓
but note WHAT it pruned on: raw frequency. "car" is gone before any strategy sees it.
STEP 4 · rankingStrategy.rank("ca", survivors, 3) — the Strategy seam
sort by freq DESC, tie-break word ASC
score is left equal to frequency
this is what the demo prints by default
no survivor is 2 chars ⇒ all boost 1.0
it only bites when the prefix IS a word:

g.text: THE ORDERING BUG WORTH ADMITTING OUT LOUD
The heap truncates to k by raw frequency, and only THEN does the RankingStrategy run. So a strategy
can re-order the survivors but can never promote a word the heap already threw away — above, "car" is
evicted at step 3, so no boost could ever bring it back into the top 3.
Fix: collect a wider candidate set (say 4×k), score with the strategy, THEN cut to k. Or let the heap's
comparator call the strategy's scorer directly, so one ordering rules the whole pipeline.

svg.text: O(L) walk + O(S) DFS + O(S log k) heap + O(k log k) rank ⇒ dominated by S, the subtree size — NOT by L.
Everything above runs inside one synchronized getSuggestions() call, so no concurrent addWord can split the walk.
Legend: orange = the prefix path · green = the DFS subtree (double ring = endOfWord) · grey = never touched
